This is fine, but FWIW we already return NOERROR on queries for these records:
```
[core@master-0 ~]$ dig api.ostest.test.metalkube.org aaaa

; <<>> DiG 9.16.23-RH <<>> api.ostest.test.metalkube.org aaaa
;; global options: +cmd
;; Got answer:
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 56859
...
```

According to CoreDNS documentation, [CoreDNS](https://coredns.io/) returns a NOERROR response code (RCODE 0)  as the default, with an empty answer section for empty responses that indicate "nodata" (name exists, but type does not). So, this change is not needed.

This will prevent you from having dual stack loadbalancers. Is that a problem?

> This will prevent you from having dual stack loadbalancers. Is that a problem?

Proper DualStack support doesn't exist now irrespective of this change. We are still in the process of adding DualStack support for these 3 platforms. Azure and GCP and in early stages, AWS is further along but not complete. 
I'll have to come back and add DualStack support in a proper way to MCO and baremetalruntime-cfg as part of feature work for DualStack. Just as with ipv4 LB addresses, we could have multiple IPv6 LB IP addresses and we can't reply on IP address ordering while rendering the Corefile template.
